clue.text: Reason to disagree with short book covering single theme

indicators.note: the short form for a volume goes round the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: BK is a standard short form of book
single means one
a theme is a topic

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an abridged volume that sticks to just one subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' says the short form of the volume wraps round the single theme; the surface's abridged book hides that BK is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a grievance to raise with someone is an idiom built on a bone that needs picking.

clue.text: Decline to indulge in chatting up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to gas is to chat idly

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join in with flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chatting up' looks like the phrase for flirting; it is GAS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or fall away, a synonym for decline as a verb.

clue.text: Garden made by old rail workers by Kent line

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now merged into the RMT
Kent is a county in South-East England, abbreviated SE
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A garden laid out by former railwaymen next to a track in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery garden is where plants are raised for sale, so the word can mean a garden.

clue.text: Drab mark on the French sort of bobsleigh

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
le is French for the
a two-man bob is one class of bobsleigh

explanation.surface: A dull scratch on a French bobsleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab' looks like an adjective meaning dull; here it is the old noun for a woman of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A drab is an archaic word for a harlot, matching the biblical phrase for an immoral woman.

clue.text: Southern county's small island

parts.note: Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A small island belonging to a county in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky island or reef, especially off Scotland.

clue.text: Puritan state into which I shall take the little woman

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the state receives the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
I shall contracts to I'll
Jo is one of the four March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A strait-laced state where a man promises to bring his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the little woman' looks like a dated phrase for a wife; it means Jo March from Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy spoils others' fun, as a puritan disapproves of pleasure.

clue.text: In professional game, be ugly — argue violently

indicators.note: violently says the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: In a professional match players behave badly and quarrel fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteen-a-side code of rugby was the professional game when union was still amateur.

clue.text: Talk about New Statesman?

indicators.note: the word for chatter goes about the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: to yak is to talk at length

explanation.surface: A discussion of the political weekly the New Statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Statesman' looks like the magazine's name; split it, and a States-man is a man from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a man of the States, a statesman is an American, informally called this.

clue.text: African and Scotsman backing landlocked republic

indicators.note: backing places the Scottish name behind the country, supporting it from the rear

parts.note: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: An African and a Scot supporting a country with no coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nigerian is a person from Nigeria, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Staff often seen with this vessel

definitions.text: Staff often seen with this vessel

parts.words: Staff often seen with this vessel
parts.note: a pole commonly carries a banner hoisted upon it, and the words for that banner and 'on' together name a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel that the staff keep near them.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff suggests employees, but it is a flagpole.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or ale.

clue.text: Climber giving gypsies pleasure

parts.note: travellers is a term for itinerant people including Gypsies
joy is great pleasure

explanation.surface: Wandering folk enjoying themselves on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wild clematis, a climbing plant common in British hedgerows.

clue.text: Bold sea cook cooked something completely unknown to me

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold ship's cook prepared a dish whose nature remains a mystery to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject you cannot understand at all is said to be one you cannot open, an idiom.

clue.text: Thick cloud approaching capital of Yemen

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud of smoke or dust

indicators.note: capital of points to the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: Dense smoke drifting towards the Yemeni capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' reads as dense cloud; it means friendly, as in thick as thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on close friendly terms with someone is to be thick with them, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Debt ready for settlement by Rupert, perhaps

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A debt ready to be paid off by someone called Rupert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for settlement' rearranges DEBT and READY; Rupert is the cartoon bear from the Daily Express.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Bear is a famous children's character who is a toy bear, an example of the type.

clue.text: Nothing vaguely careless about cook

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the zero, holding it
vaguely says the letters are put together loosely in a different order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook who is neither vague nor careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' rearranges CARELESS, and 'about' puts that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat slowly in a covered dish is to make a stew of this kind, used as a verb.

clue.text: Raise joint, lifting away from one direction but to another

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting reads the word upwards

indicators.text: away from one direction but to another
indicators.note: the compass point west is taken away and another bearing, north-north-east, put in its place

parts.note: the elbow is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: Someone raises a joint and moves it from one bearing to another.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes and NNE replaces it, giving ELBONNE, which 'lifting' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage, or elevate them in dignity.

clue.text: Extremely large girl is above board

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A very big girl is honest and open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful is permitted and so is open and honest in its dealings.

clue.text: Hat on and cape

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: Put a hat on and a cape too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link; in cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A leghorn is a straw hat made from plaited Italian wheat straw.

clue.text: Prophylactic treatment provided by hospital department in Headingley, possibly

indicators.note: in puts the hospital department inside the rearranged place name
possibly signals the letters could be ordered another way

parts.note: Headingley is a district of Leeds known for its cricket ground
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Preventive care offered by a hospital unit in Headingley, a part of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of the place name, and 'in' says the department sits inside it; the surface makes Headingley a real hospital location.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning teeth to prevent decay is preventive care, the kind of protection the word prophylactic describes.

clue.text: David, for instance, is somewhat affected

definitions.meaning: ... David is the US president's country retreat, so it is an example of a ...
affected and theatrical in manner, exaggerated in style

explanation.definitionFit: Camp means exaggerated or mannered behaviour, and Camp David is a retreat.

clue.text: A second president overthrown by insignificant creature

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: overthrown turns the president's short name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Abe is short for Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Someone briefly in power is toppled by a nonentity.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism is tiny, so it serves as an example of an insignificant creature.

clue.text: It's seen in dance backed by someone like Pyrrho

indicators.note: backed says the whole assembly is read backwards
the letters of it's are seen inside the dance

parts.note: the conga is a dance done in a line
it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something spotted at a dance with the support of a Greek philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' says the dance holds the clue's opening word, and 'backed' turns the whole run round. Pyrrho was a Greek philosopher who founded scepticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrrho held that nothing can be known for certain, which matches one who holds that God cannot be known.

clue.text: Drink for a child

explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits and also a small child.

clue.text: Having less room to manoeuvre one interrupts game

indicators.note: the numeral breaks into the card game, sitting inside it

parts.note: poker is a card game
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Feeling cramped when someone barges into a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pokier compares rooms that are smaller and more cramped, leaving little space.

clue.text: Maid hurries back and starts to spring-clean the entire room

indicators.note: back says the word for hurries is read in reverse

parts.note: to nip is to hurry somewhere briefly

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A housemaid rushes back and begins a thorough spring clean of the whole room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIPS to SPIN, and 'starts to' gives STER.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman was traditionally called an old maid, so maid serves as a synonym.
